name: Amendment #3 application accepted for review
body: The Environmental Assessment Office has accepted Cedar LNG Partners LP’s application to amend Environmental Assessment Certificate E23-01. The amendment would change the marine terminal design and extend the construction window by 18 months. A public comment period on the draft Application Information Requirements opens on 11 February 2026 and runs for 30 days. The assessment team will respond to the issues raised in its assessment report, which is published with the decision record.

name: Comment period open on draft Application Information Requirements
body: Comment on the draft Application Information Requirements, which set out what the proponent must study and report on in its amendment application. Comments are considered by the assessment team and published with the decision record. The period closes at 11:59 pm on 13 March 2026.

name: Inspection record published
body: Findings from the January site visit are available in the inspection record below. The inspection found the project in compliance with all conditions inspected, with one advisory issued regarding sediment control at the marine terminal laydown area.

name: Readiness decision issued
body: The Chief Executive Assessment Officer has determined that the project description meets the requirements to proceed to process planning. The reasons for the decision are published with the record, together with the summary of engagement that informed it.

name: Process order issued
body: The order sets out how the assessment will be conducted, which parties participate, and the time limits that apply to each stage of the process. It also confirms the methods the proponent must use to assess effects on caribou habitat.

name: Effects assessment begins
body: The assessment team has begun evaluating the potential effects of the project, working with participating Indigenous nations, technical advisors and local governments. This stage carries a legislated time limit of 150 days.

name: Certificate issued with 38 conditions
body: Ministers have issued an environmental assessment certificate for the project. The certificate carries 38 legally binding conditions covering water quality, wildlife habitat, air emissions and reclamation. Compliance with each condition is monitored by the Environmental Assessment Office and reported publicly.

name: Public comment period closed
body: The comment period on the application closed on 30 September. All submissions are published, and the assessment team will respond to the issues raised in the assessment report.

name: Application accepted for review
body: The application has been accepted as complete and moves into review. The review considers whether the application meets the information requirements set during process planning, and runs to a legislated limit of 180 days.

name: Enforcement action concluded
body: The compliance and enforcement branch has closed its file on the sediment control matter reported in March. The proponent completed the required remediation and reporting, and no further action is planned.
